sections.heading: PQ Devnet 0 and Devnet 1 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 0 is stable after initial fixes; devnet 1 launched during the call with all 8 CL clients, adding staggered aggregations.
sections.body:
- Devnet 0 has been running stably for a couple of days after initial issues with XMSS/VRF key loading logic and caching were resolved.
- The VRF key format changed in leanVM version 0.19; Kurtosis testing has been done with the new format.
- Devnet 1 launched 6 minutes before the update; some Silver nodes were unable to propose blocks, under investigation.
- The only major difference between devnet 0 and devnet 1 is staggered aggregations, expected to be implemented by every client.
- All 8 CL clients are running on both devnet 0 and devnet 1.
- Monitoring via Dora and Xatu for aggregation and attestation times is being set up; expected to be available same day.
  - Barnabas requested clients expose aggregation times in `/metrics` so tooling can consume them.
- Devnet 0 was shut down during the call.
- ethlambda merged multiple performance improvements on the validator client for devnet 0 and is porting them to devnet 1.
  - Images are auto-built, enabling fast feedback.
- Devnet has ~20 nodes currently; a larger test planned once initial issues are ironed out.
- Testing with 16 small committees proposed to get representative 16-to-1 recursion without needing 700K validators.
  - Generating 700K keys would take ~60 days and require ~1,400 nodes at 500 keys per host.
  - Agreement that clients should modify setups to have fewer validators per committee but more committees.
  - Francesco D'Amato suggested testing recursion in one devnet with small committees and aggregation in another with a single large committee.

sections.heading: Spec Stability
sections.summary: Specs are considered stable with no changes needed to answer the PQ Gasper feasibility question; no objections raised.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray stated specs are currently stable and no additions are needed to investigate whether PQ Gasper should be pursued.
- No objections or comments were raised by any participants.
- Barnabas confirmed agreement.

sections.heading: leanVM Performance and Freezing
sections.summary: leanVM v0.19 achieves 2.2s for 16-to-1 recursion on NUC 14 Pro (4 cores); clients want larger-scale testing before freezing performance targets.
sections.body:
- Latest leanVM version is 0.19, which restores 8 XMSS subtrees cached by default but makes the number configurable (clients can choose 4).
- Performance on NUC 14 Pro: 16-to-1 recursion on 4 cores takes 2.2 seconds with machine otherwise idle.
  - With EVM execution on remaining cores, estimated ~25% overhead, keeping it below 3 seconds in practice.
  - Benchmarks available at [leanvm.org](https://leanvm.org/).
- Tom Wambsgans requested that if performance is good enough, the team can shift focus to security, stability, and auditability.
- Silver (Alexey) raised concern that devnet testing with ~10K validators is not representative of mainnet's far larger validator set, and leanVM needs testing under proper load with more aggregators.
  - On current devnets, only 2 committees exist instead of 16, so 16-to-1 recursion is not being tested.
- Tom clarified committee size has less than 10% impact on 16-to-1 recursion time, so small committees with 16 committees would give near-mainnet-representative recursion numbers.
- Alexey estimated needing roughly 10-20% improvement for XMSS aggregation; wants real numbers before confirming.
- Kevaundray: if leanVM needs a 2x improvement, the likely answer is Decoupled Consensus (DC) rather than trying to extract more performance.
- For XMSS mass aggregation bottleneck, two options exist: sacrifice DVT-friendliness for ~1.5-2x speedup, or implement top-layer caching/pre-aggregation (more complexity).
- Tom noted for recursion, a 10% improvement (doable) would suffice on NUC 14 Pro; for XMSS, a 2x would be needed via either less DVT friendliness or caching.
- Yann Vonlanthen noted that due to pipelining, aggregation performance on leanVM itself is unlikely to be the bottleneck in DC; networking is more likely the constraint.
- Kamil suggested 2K sigs/second with 16-to-1 in 2 seconds should be good enough.
- Mikhail noted DC provides more room to work around leanVM performance numbers than PQ Gasper does.

sections.heading: Staking Contracts
sections.summary: Pre-registry contract ~4 months from mainnet, blocked on the XMSS spec freeze (end of January); Tau takes the deposit contract, EIP-8205 and voluntary exits.
sections.body:
- Ignacio shared status document ([EIP-8483 workstream status](https://hackmd.io/@jsign/eip-8483-workstream-status)) covering all main pieces of the staking contracts.
- Timeline: contracts deploy before H-star fork so validators/builders can pre-register PQ material; at H-star, system calls begin dequeuing; at I-star, remaining BLS validators are ejected.
- All relevant artifacts are in place: system contracts in sys-asm repo, XMSS signature verification in a separate repo, EIP description, consensus spec branch, and a newly opened execution spec branch.
- System contract architecture follows existing queue-based system contracts with tunings; differences documented for auditing ramp-up.
- Open questions remain in two categories:
  - System contract architecture questions — need input from sys-asm owners or EF architecture/Steel team.
  - CL-related questions about constants.
- Auditing has two parts:
  - Queue contracts: can be audited as soon as architecture decisions are finalized.
  - XMSS EVM bytecode verifier: blocked on XMSS spec freeze, expected end of January; has test vectors and ongoing formal verification by Tomas, but likely also needs an external audit.
- Estimated mainnet deployment: ~4 months from now; main blocker is XMSS spec freeze since deployed contracts cannot be changed.
- Action: LightClient and Steel team to be pinged async to begin reviewing the non-XMSS parts.
- EIP-8205 update for PQ:
  - Dima (Lido) confirmed willingness to collaborate; Tau (Francesco Risitano) will lead and coordinate with Lido.
  - Lido can jump in starting next week if needed.
- Voluntary exit contract (moving voluntary exits to EL, triggered by operator signing with validator key):
  - Tau to lead this work as well.
  - Dima requested that the pre-PQ message format not change to avoid signer changes; post-PQ it can be redesigned since all signers change anyway.
- Consolidations and withdrawal-credential-triggered exits: no contract changes needed, only semantic changes.

sections.heading: Networking Simulations and Protocol Comparisons
sections.summary: Three independent simulation efforts are underway comparing GossipSub, seacast, and simpler segmented broadcasting; confident cross-checked results targeted for Friday next week.
sections.body:
- Csaba is running simulations using the Go codebase, simulating attestation and aggregation phases with mainnet-realistic parameters, with work-in-progress runs of up to 1,000 nodes.
  - Each simulation run takes ~5 hours; multiple runs with different seeds needed for statistical significance.
  - Work-in-progress results exist but are not reviewed; confident results targeted for end of next week (Friday).
  - Running the GossipSub baseline and a lightly modified GossipSub variant without segmentation.
  - Csaba checked numbers during the call and confirmed GossipSub baseline numbers "are bad."
- Kamil is running parallel simulations comparing GossipSub, seacast, and a simpler announce-and-pull protocol.
  - Announce-and-pull surprisingly performed well in some simulations.
  - Has proof broadcast simulation results published at a [report page](https://kamilsa.github.io/leansim/reports/proof-propagation-report.html).
  - Found seacast spec too large and not widely understood; simpler approaches showed comparable or better performance.
  - Has Lighthouse fork implementing proof broadcast protocol on top of Waggle; Teku also working on it.
  - Lighthouse and Teku interop on fast proof broadcast expected early next week.
- Anton also ran simulations with somewhat controversial results differing across runs.
  - Found JVM and Rust GossipSub implementations differ in ways that matter for results.
  - Current GossipSub numbers "not that bad" but acknowledges this may reflect an optimized GossipSub variant.
- Yann shared simulations pointing to GossipSub not being good enough for PQ Gasper: [write-up](https://github.com/yannvon/dc-networking/blob/main/posts/pq-gasper-on-gossipsub.md).
- jxs (Waggle co-author, GossipSub maintainer) noted GossipSub doesn't support chunking in-protocol; once you chunk proofs, a chunking-aware protocol (Waggle or GossipSub partial messages) is more appropriate.
- Mikhail noted that chunking undermines the "seen superset" optimization for aggregates (discarding aggregates with fewer bits than already seen), though staggered aggregate propagation could mitigate this.
- Vlad reported seacast over GossipSub for envelopes and aggregates is implemented in Silver and Prysm; aggregates use ~40% less bandwidth vs. plain GossipSub.
  - Some latency increase with superset check on chunks.
- Agreement that simulation methodology needs alignment before drawing conclusions; 30% differences observed between simulators due to link-layer modeling differences.
- Target: simulation results with cross-checked confidence by Friday next week; simulations need to be done by Tuesday/Wednesday.
- Francesco Risitano (Tau) suggested framing the question as "what leanVM performance do we need" for each regime rather than taking leanVM as fixed.

sections.heading: Network Specs Repository
sections.summary: New ethereum/network-specs repository created as a canonical location for networking specifications; teams asked to file issues pointing to their specs.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray created a new repository: [ethereum/network-specs](https://github.com/ethereum/network-specs).
- Purpose: centralize networking specs that are currently scattered across ERCs, consensus specs, and various notes.
- Csaba confirmed this is a long-planned fix; they want to do it properly, which takes time.
- Teams asked to open issues in the repo pointing to where their protocol specs live (Waggle, Kamil's protocol, seacast variants).
- Felix is expected to migrate additional content to the repo.

sections.heading: ERC-8517 Review and Key Lifetime Assumption
sections.summary: ERC-8517 merged automatically; a follow-up PR will address Gottfried's review. Its key store assumes keys never run out, worth revisiting if XMSS changes.
sections.body:
- Manu confirmed the [ERC-8517](https://github.com/ethereum/ERCs/blob/master/ERCS/erc-8517.md) was merged; Gottfried reviewed it after automatic merging.
- Manu and Thomas Coratger will open a new PR to incorporate Gottfried's review comments.
- Gottfried flagged a broader concern: the key store design and ERC writing implicitly assume key lifetime exceeds everything the system cares about (i.e., keys never run out of material).
  - If XMSS spec changes shrink key lifetime drastically, this assumption would need to be reconsidered.
  - The XMSS leaf corresponds to a slot; wrapping around is possible but not currently accounted for in the ERC.
  - This concern is orthogonal to the specific review comments.

- Call cadence reduced from 3 per week to 2 per week.

sections.heading: Networking Devnet Planning
sections.summary: Two parallel devnet tracks proposed: Silver/Prysm testing seacast-over-GossipSub, and Lighthouse/Teku testing Kamil's segmented broadcast protocol over Waggle.
sections.body:
- Barnabas proposed running devnets with segmented broadcasting protocols for A/B comparison against GossipSub baseline, using the same node count and validator setup.
- Current implementation landscape:
  - Silver and Prysm: seacast over GossipSub implemented (for envelopes and aggregates, not proof broadcast specifically in Prysm).
  - Lighthouse and Teku: implementing Kamil's fast proof broadcast protocol ([spec](https://notes.ethereum.org/@kamilsa/rk_I4TMJme)), expected early next week.
  - ethlambda: testing payload dissemination via Waggle.
  - Prysm also has a Waggle implementation (by Sukun), but not for proofs.
- Kamil clarified seacast is not built on top of Waggle; his protocol is distinct and needs a name ("Woof" jokingly proposed).
- Csaba noted seacast-over-Waggle is specified but not yet implemented; seacast-over-GossipSub is implemented.
- Vlad suggested running two separate devnets: Silver/Prysm pair and Lighthouse/Teku pair, each testing their respective protocol, then comparing results.
- Barnabas requested all networking implementations be rebased on devnet 1 spec (not devnet 0).
- Barnabas confirmed scope: only aggregation proofs go through alternative P2P stack; everything else stays on GossipSub.
- Barnabas noted client confusion about what exactly to implement; Csaba commented that studies before devnets would have helped.
- Agreed to add segmented broadcasting of aggregation proofs to the next devnet; which protocol(s), and whether to run one devnet per track, to be settled async and on next week's P2P call.
- Kamil emphasized implementation complexity should factor into protocol decisions alongside performance numbers.
